A.best_element: Personal-use GCP setup guide, including publishing the OAuth app to 'In production' to escape the 7-day Testing refresh-token expiry, plus the base32hex event-ID gotcha (e.g. 'sgw' is invalid)
A.biggest_weakness: Lopsided toward Google auth: highlight/hide, sniping and the explicit SGW ToS ban get a single bullet each, so the plan will be thin exactly where the money and account risk lives

B.best_element: Honest T0/T1/T2 reliability tiers ('a daily check can catch up, a snipe cannot') combined with contracts frozen in Phase 0 behind SgwClient/ListingCardAdapter isolation
B.biggest_weakness: Calls the SGW ToS stance 'unverified' (it explicitly bans browser extensions), steers clock sync to Dashboard/GetCurrentTime (second resolution), and asserts the MV3 'background' permission keeps Chrome alive without flagging it

C.best_element: Test-only hooks compiled out of production with a CI check proving it, runtime schema validation that fails closed, and a threat-model table mapping each control to the test that proves it
C.biggest_weakness: Treats the ToS as unknown, has a stale Firefox host-permission claim, gives little snipe-timing guidance, and a long non-negotiable process list risks a ceremony-heavy plan

D.best_element: Site Adapter (Dom/Api/Session/Clock) with versioned selectors and endpoints and a healthCheck() that disables all write automation on drift, fed by a read-only recon Task 0 that settles soft-close empirically and produces all fixtures
D.biggest_weakness: Specifies Playwright e2e on Firefox (unsupported for extensions) and gives thin snipe-engine detail: no lead-time default, no ambiguous-response/no-retry rule, no total-exposure cap

E.best_element: Flags that auto-favoriting may attract rival bidders, so auto-favorite becomes a per-watch choice with a local-only watch alternative; plus never-silent hiding with 'Why?' and one-click undo
E.biggest_weakness: States unverified claims as fact ('no clock extension', the 15-auction new-account cap, ~6 s competitor snipes, 500-char notes) and is a UX spec 'treated as requirements', inviting scope creep and an over-prescribed plan

rationale: D beat C because its SGW facts are current and actionable: the exact ToS text, serverTime with ms versus GetCurrentTime at 1 s, the Bid-cookie 403 / credentials:'omit' gotcha, a likely IP/UA-bound JWT, and the naive-PT endTime. It also requires a fail-closed Site Adapter health check and a fixture-producing recon spike that settles soft-close empirically, which is exactly the base an orchestrator of isolated agents needs. C has the stronger testing discipline, but it treats the ToS as unknown, carries a stale Firefox permissions claim and gives little snipe-timing guidance, so a plan built from it is more likely to miss the real-world risks.
